    Kobre Gearwardens¶

    [!INFO] The Interlocking Guard — Steel That Fits A purse that meshes. A line that holds. A gear that will not slip.

    History¶

    The military order of Kobre — a continent south of the Formingar Ocean whose isolation let Hybrians try to take it with Homunculi as agents, and whose liberation came by accident when Baoth's destruction in the Great Divergence shattered the psychic link and the Homunculi awoke free under the Unnamed (later Omipre). The Gearwardens were born in the stabilization that followed centuries of starving war.

    Kobre holds four nations — Homunculi Kingdom (the free homunculi), Coalsteel and Diamonds (dwarf kingdoms — Diamonds built a wall against the Homunculi), and Elf Kingdom (elven exiles). The Gearwardens are the only formation drawn from all four in practice if not in name: homunculi-forged, dwarf-tested, elven-carried. Their founding charter was a milling-tolerance agreement. Their first battle was holding a pass while a gear-forge was moved behind the Diamonds wall. They hold that a war won without the forge running is a war paid for in forge-winter later.

    Every homunculus still trains in combat from youth; every Coalsteel dwarf still knows how to hold a line; the Gearwardens are what happens when both remember how at the same time.

    Patron¶

    The Homunculi Kingdom as institution — and through it, the memory of the Unnamed / Omipre, who taught that abandonment by their Silver Bride-calling god did not require abandonment of each other. Formally the Gearwardens are attested by the Coalsteel furnaces and Diamond presses; spiritually they are homunculi communal — no one eats alone, no one holds alone. The Gearwardens' pre-battle shared meal is eaten from one pot, gear-teeth clacking as bowls mesh.

    Entry is mutual and banned in mirror: Homunculi are banned from Coalsteel, Diamonds, and Elf Kingdom; outsiders are unwelcome in the Homunculi lands. The Gearwardens are the exception both sides grant because they have seen the alternative.

    Sigil¶

    An interlocking gear and a crossed hammer-pike on a soot-gray field edged in diamond-white. The gear's tooth count signals company: 12-tooth for line, 24 for veteran, 36 for command, 48 for the forge-guard that never leaves the hobber hall. Counterfeit insignia is instantly detectable — real Gearwarden gears mesh and turn; fakes jam. Engineers literally use retired insignia as gears in the field, a fact both dwarves and homunculi consider not improvisation but proof of design.

    Role¶

    Precision defense and industrial security. The Gearwardens hold the walls and passes between the Homunculi and dwarven kingdoms, protect the furnace valleys and the The Groom-ward coast of Kobre that still draws [Black Agent|black dust] curiosities, and — critically — guard the fabrication chain that makes the continent's wealth: Coalsteel furnaces, Diamond presses, water-powered hobbers that cut gears to 0.02mm. A Gearwarden line that breaks is not a lost position but a broken supply: every retreat is therefore a re-convergence on the next forge, not a rout.

    They loan companies to Kutten smiths at Malbodor who import Kobre steel, and those smiths in turn send Kutten Fang scalps back as receipts — a quiet alliance measured in steel quality, not speeches.

    Relation to Currencies & Regions¶

    The Gearwardens are the guard behind the Kobran Gear — gear-shaped steel discs where teeth count is denomination, forged by the Homunculi Kingdom to absurd tolerance. Backed by Coalsteel furnaces, Kobre fabrication, and the fact that a counterfeit gear jams a purse — the most literal proof-of-work on Ge'or. The four Kobre nations all use Gear, and even Elf Kingdom exiles adopted it for trade.

    For foreign dealings the Gearwardens convert through Demon's Horn and Beast's Bay to Vennerian Ducat for sea freight, and to Kutten Fang via Malbodor for mineral trade; their reserve is steel itself — ingots stamped with gear-tooth edges so a purse of reserves can literally rebuild a hobber.
